verification.note: frontend/src/__tests__/uploadProcessingRefresh.test.tsx:74-89 renderCompleted drops only a.txt (file_a). The it.each at :259-307 asserts callsSoFar[1] equals [["file_a"]] (:299). The only queued follow-up is replayed at frontend/src/hooks/useUpload.ts:264-268. If it instead queued {all:true} (useUpload.ts:234), refreshProcessingOnce (:280-292) would choose every entry that needsProcessingFetch, and with one entry that is still ["file_a"]. The assertion passes either way. The other tests that touch mid-request or processing (uploadProcessingView.test.tsx, uploadLock.test.tsx) do not exercise a mid-request event with several entries, so nothing would catch that regression.

This is the same gap as R4-1. The 'a held id' case (uploadProcessingRefresh.test.tsx:261) runs with a single entry from renderCompleted (:86), and :299 expects ["file_a"]. A mutation of queueProcessingRefresh (useUpload.ts:237-249) that sets processingRefreshQueued = { all: true } whenever held.length > 0 would replay refreshProcessing() with no ids (:267). That still requests only file_a, because it is the only entry needing a fetch (:281-285), so the test would pass.

specification_compliance: The code follows I8 (r2) id scoping for queued mid-request refreshes. queueProcessingRefresh keeps only held ids that still need a fetch, and the follow-up replays only those ids (useUpload.ts:237-249, 264-268). What is missing is a test with more than one entry.
regression_risks: A mid-request follow-up that widens to every entry would go unnoticed, because no test drives a mid-request event with two or more entries.
test_coverage: The it.each in uploadProcessingRefresh.test.tsx:259-307 covers a foreign id (no follow-up) and a held id (one follow-up), each with one entry only. It does not cover id narrowing among several entries.
not_verified: I did not run the test suite or a mutation; the claims were checked by reading the code only.
I did not review test files outside frontend/src/__tests__ for multi-entry mid-request coverage.
